enumeration.method: Independent small-caps THEOREM-heading enumeration on PDF1–22 and visual review of both full statements and all prerequisite passages.

checks: Pinned title, all three authors, arXiv version/date, 73-page count and both PDF hashes verified. All 22 archived main-text pages match fresh PDF extraction byte for byte; page22 funding and the next-page S1 heading establish the boundary.
Independent small-caps heading enumeration confirms exactly two Theorems and excludes ordinary-font references. Both full statements remain unchanged from their separately validated inventory.

The exact parameter restrictions, conditional minimax risk, logarithmic powers, rate denominator and missing-pattern indicator were compared with the original theorem pages. The HAM theorem retains the plus class and its own weaker parameter restrictions.

All 30 source members, their naming contexts, all 21 algorithm lines and six ambient passages were checked against rendered main-text pages. Bold vectors, script classes, Bayes superscript and pattern-indexed scalar exponents were checked against source typesetting.

The experiment uses incomplete training records and a complete unconditional test point. Joint and marginal laws, prescribed masks and observed available patterns, and conditional versus unconditional projected feature measures remain distinct.

The anova recursion, signal lower bound, antichains and predecessor/complement sets, lower-density condition, smoothness and margin classes preserve their original formulas and quantifiers. No independent-coordinate or ordinary-density assumption is inserted.

Independent dependency expectations confirm 25 direct uses and 57 related connections. The minimax theorem has no HAM algorithm or Definition3+ dependency. HAM numerical steps do not consume population interaction or signal values.

Algorithm neighbor-count and pattern-selection ambiguities are checked against the literal formulas, including simple n_omega=1 and incomparable-pattern examples. Zero exponents, projection/index inconsistencies and unspecified tie/order conventions remain recorded separately.

Empty compatible-mask minima and empty extrema in Theorem1 lack an explicit main-text convention and remain unresolved. Supplementary proofs and alternative definitions were not used to silently fill gaps.

Every interface has source-backed natural-language keywords, source identity, meaningful highlight selectors and explanations for every related theorem path. Math delimiters and braces, main-text evidence bounds and artifact hashes are checked; inventory and census validators pass.

source_notes: Pinned arXiv:2305.11672v2, 73 pages, dated 2 May 2024. Main text PDF1–22 ends in funding; Sections S1–S5 starting on PDF23 and following references are excluded. Exact final-journal equivalence is not asserted.
Two actual main-text Theorems are preserved in full. Main-text Propositions 3–6 and supplementary Lemmas/Propositions/Theorems are not added to the Theorem inventory.

Training triples are iid; only masked features, full labels and masks are observed. The test point is fully observed and has the unconditional marginal P_Q, not the conditional complete-case distribution.
The theorem expectations condition on every training mask. Positive probability is required for each specified o in O; the source does not require Q to put zero mask mass outside O.
Masking leaves vectors in R^d with zero-filled coordinates. The mask distinguishes an observed zero from an unobserved coordinate. Lower-density dimension d_omega may differ from this ambient d.

The original missingness assumption equates subvector regression probabilities at all support points and all compatible masks. It allows dependence and examples of missing not at random; it is not replaced by an MCAR assumption.

Pointwise conditional probabilities and conditional expectations are used outside an almost-everywhere formulation. The source does not explicitly fix versions everywhere on support; no version regularity is added.

The anova recursion subtracts all strict-predecessor components inside the conditional expectation, with a centered constant component. The source describes these functions as orthogonal without imposing independent feature coordinates in the general setup. The recursion and description are retained without certifying that assertion or substituting a different decomposition.
The signal sigma_omega^2 is a conditional second moment minimized over compatible masks, not a centered variance. It may be zero in the minimax theorem because c_E=0 is allowed; HAM requires c_E>0.
Minima over compatible masks occur in the signal and tail definitions even for patterns not contained in any o in O. No explicit empty-minimum convention is given in the inspected main text.

U(Omega) is the complement of Omega and its strict lower closure, so it includes incomparable patterns. It is not only the strict upper closure. The displayed braces around the removed union are preserved as printed grouping.

The unconditional masked measure mu_omega and conditional training measure mu_{omega|o} remain distinct. Definition 3 evaluates conditional lower-density events under the unconditional test measure; Definition 3+ additionally uses every conditional measure on the outside.
Lower density uses open balls and radii 0<r<1; its exponent can be less than ambient dimension. It does not require an ordinary density or a uniform positive bound.
The margin event is |eta-1/2|<t and includes exact ties; no additional 0<|eta-1/2| restriction is inserted. Bayes and HAM both choose class one at a tie.
Counts n_omega are the number of containing realized masks, not exact-pattern counts or expected counts. Script N and prescribed script O have different meanings.

Theorem 1 allows Omega_star intersect N to be empty. Then the printed definition of R and the minimum inside its logarithm have empty domains, with no explicit convention in the main text. The unavailable-pattern indicator communicates the intended constant-risk regime but does not define those empty extrema.

Theorem 1 retains its exact lower-bound-only margin and constant restrictions. Its upper bound adds the unavailable-pattern indicator outside the C times logarithmic rate product. The constants may depend on class parameters but not n or the realized mask sequence.

Theorem 2 uses C_L>=1 while the introductory domain for Q-prime-Miss in (11) states C_L>1. Definition 3 and Definition 3+ allow C_L>=1; the plus-class replacement implicitly extends that introductory domain, without changing the original text.

Algorithm 1 uses k_omega=1+floor(n_omega^a) without capping at n_omega. At n_omega=1 this requests two neighbors from one available case. Theorem 2 does not impose a lower sample size on active and lower patterns. Main-text Section 5.2 separately writes k_omega in [n_omega] for its proof quantities but does not change Algorithm 1 or supply a cap.

Algorithm 1 admits zero coordinate tail parameters. For processed patterns with gamma_omega=0 and alpha=0, its tuning exponents have zero numerator and denominator. Positivity on active patterns alone does not explicitly cover coordinates outside their union.

Algorithm 1 line 7 calls projected feature/label pairs a reordering of pairs retaining the original masks o_i. The first last-neighbor X subscript also omits the pattern index that appears in the corresponding distance expression. Both printed forms are preserved.

Algorithm 1 loops over evaluations at X_i^{o_i} and x0, but line 10 evaluates fitted components at X_i^omega. Its intended dependence only on x^omega makes those compatible conceptually; the printed finite evaluation loop does not explicitly implement that extension.

Algorithm 1 line 15 requires U({omega}) intersect hat-Omega to be empty. Because U includes incomparable patterns, this condition can suppress incomparable candidates after one is selected, unlike the prose that says only predecessors are disregarded. No corrected set condition is substituted.

Nearest-neighbor distance ties and the traversal order of equal-dimensional patterns are unspecified. Combined with the printed selection condition, different within-level orders can select different surviving incomparable patterns.

Algorithm 1 line 2 writes a bold zero subscript without d; this is retained rather than silently changing it to the population notation f_{0_d}. The reconstruction excludes the constant term if hat-Omega is empty, as printed.

Theorem 2 sample-size condition uses an ordinary logarithm with the full exponent 4[gamma_omega(2 beta_omega+d_omega)+alpha beta_omega]/(beta_omega gamma_omega). Its conclusion uses log-plus=log(max(x,e)), not log(1+x).

The HAM procedure is stored as one complete algorithmic definition; its inline temporary quantities are not split into invented population interfaces. The oracle algorithm, Assouad lemma and proof concentration events are not imported into statement dependencies.

unresolved_source_references.reference: Proposition S1 and Lemma S2, Section S1.1
unresolved_source_references.resolution: Supplementary explanations of the missingness class are not read; Definition1 itself is complete in the main text.
The recursion and reconstruction are stated in the main text; supplementary claims or proofs of orthogonality are not imported.
Supplementary proof of HAM risk bound excluded; full Algorithm1 and statement retained.

ambient_resolution.shared: D3 defines Q and the unconditional test-pair law P_Q; D4 gives eta and mu. D5 fixes iid incomplete training records and a complete test feature vector. The outer theorem expectation conditions on the entire mask sequence, whose event has positive probability by D10. Script O is a prescribed set of mask values with positive probabilities, not necessarily the entire mask support; script N in D26 is the downward-closed set supported by the realized sample. D1 resolves pattern dimension and componentwise order; D2 is a zero-filled R^d vector, not an R^{d_omega} vector. D15 is the antichain domain; D16 defines L and U, including incomparable patterns in U. Bold beta/gamma denote coordinate vectors; D19,D21 define unbolded patternwise minima. D27 specifies log-plus as log(max(x,e)). A1,A2 fix elementary indices, constant vectors, Euclidean norm and open balls. Indicator functions, supports, probability measures, conditional expectations, measurable maps, complement relative to the Boolean universe, infima/suprema, integer floors and finite sums are ambient. No independent-coordinate, MCAR or MAR assumption is silently imposed. Conditional versions at every support point and minima over empty mask sets remain source convention issues.
ambient_resolution.1: Theorem 1 ranges over all D6 classifiers and the prime intersection class D24. Its constituents are the missingness condition D10, interaction class D17 from recursive anova D11 and conditional signal D14, lower-density tail class D20 based on D12 unconditional and D13 conditional measures plus D18 lower density, smoothness D22 and margin D23. The loss is D9, resolved through D7 conditional test error and D8 Bayes rule, with the unconditional test distribution A4. R is defined completely inline; its inputs D25 counts, D26 available patterns, D1 dimensions, D19 tail exponents and D21 smoothness exponents are separate prerequisites. The unavailable-pattern indicator appears on both sides, with its upper-bound occurrence outside C times the log-rate product. c,C are locally existential and independent of sample size and mask values, not asserted independent of all class parameters. c_E includes zero, C_L>1 and all lower-bound-specific constant/margin restrictions are preserved. Neither Algorithm 1 nor Definition 3+ is a statement prerequisite of this minimax assertion. If Omega_star intersect N is empty, the printed R maximum and logarithmic minimum lack an explicit convention in the main text; the indicator does not define those quantities.
ambient_resolution.2: Theorem 2 uses the plus class D30: its intersection ingredients are inherited from D24 with D29 replacing the tail class and retaining (9). The extra condition uses every compatible conditional training measure on the outside, in addition to the unconditional measure control. D28 preserves all 21 lines of the HAM algorithm, including residual estimates, neighbor size, thresholds, empirical signal, descending pattern selection and final reconstruction. Numeric computation of that algorithm does not consume population anova components or sigma values; those appear through its statistical model class. The sample-size condition runs only over U(Omega_star) intersect N from D16,D26; all active patterns must be available. It uses ordinary log, while the risk bound uses D27 log-plus. c_E is positive and C_L>=1. Theorem 1 restrictions max alpha beta<=min dimension, c_E<=1/(16|Omega_star|), and large lower-bound constants are not imported. Algorithm parameters use D19,D21 exponents for every processed nonzero pattern, creating unresolved zero-gamma cases outside the active set when alpha is also zero. The specified k_omega can exceed n_omega at n_omega=1. The original U({omega}) selection condition conflicts with A5 for incomparable candidates; nearest-neighbor ties and within-level traversal order are not specified. These are saved as source issues rather than repaired. Proposition 6 and supplementary proofs are not theorem statement prerequisites.

review_limits: Source transcription and statement-dependency audit, not proof certification or correction of source errors.
Pinned preprint inspected; final journal equivalence is not asserted.
Supplementary Sections S1–S5 excluded. Empty-extremum conventions and printed algorithm ambiguities remain unresolved as documented.

registered_source_correction.description: Correct one Python escape in D19 naming_context: backspace plus oldsymbol is restored to the source LaTeX command for the bold tail vector. Original statements, definitions, dependency paths and counts are unchanged.
